title: introduce-v1-compat-parameter-bridge-and-toolcall-framing
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a compatibility layer (v1 parameter bridge) that maps OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parameters into Redwood's internal request model and runtime hints. Motivation: customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs expect consistent behavior for stops, roles, logprobs, and tool/function-calling semantics; without a dedicated bridge we observed drift in edge-cases and streaming failure modes. Key features: 1) parameter_bridge: central normalization for temperature/top_p/n and role aliases with precedence rules; 2) adaptive_stop: new stop weighting that preserves explicit stop arrays but allows runtime fallback when models return token-level logprob gaps; 3) logprob_fallback: when model variants do not emit dense logprobs we synthesize conservative token-prob approximations and mark them with a provenance header; 4) toolcall_framing: consistent framed-tool envelope used over streaming so partial tool outputs are discoverable and reassembled deterministically by clients; 5) stream_heartbeat: a small keepalive ping added to long-lived streams to avoid intermediate proxies closing connections (configurable and off by default); 6) response_normalizer: structured output post-processing that enforces v1 expected shapes (choices[].message.role/ content/finish_reason and choice-level logprobs when available). Backwards compatibility: default bridge behavior preserves existing Redwood semantics unless request explicitly sets v1_compat=true. Migration notes: customers using custom stop heuristics should test with the new weighted_stop param and may opt into legacy_stop_mode. Performance: added lightweight routing hints only; measured median latency change <1% p95 stable due to additional small allocations. Testing: unit tests for mapping logic, end-to-end streaming integration tests including simulated proxy timeouts, and compatibility tests against the openai-compat conformance harness. See commits for file-level changes and reviewer thread for addressed comments.

feat(streaming): implement stream_heartbeat and keepalive framing
feat(tooling): toolcall framed envelope and reassembly logic
fix(stop): preserve explicit stop array precedence, add weighted_stop fallback
test: add e2e compatibility suite and proxy simulation tests
docs: document v1_compat flags and migration guide
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can we centralize role aliasing in a single table instead of ad-hoc mappings? Response: yes — consolidated into param_bridge.role_map and added unit tests (see commit 3)
Samir Patel: Concern about adding heartbeat by default since some customers rely on proxy timeouts. Response: heartbeat is opt-in via config and default=off; updated README and flags.
Rosa Kim: Suggest adding provenance header for synthesized logprobs so downstream evals know they are approximations. Response: added X-Redwood-Logprob-Provenance and test coverage.
CI: lint flagged imports in framing.go; fixed in follow-up commit and re-ran CI (green).
QA: e2e sim reproduced a corner case where partial tool outputs were dropped; fixed by ensuring chunk sequence numbers are strictly increasing and added replay test.
release_notes: v1 compatibility: introduce parameter bridge for /v1/chat.completions mapping, stable tool/function call framing for streaming, adaptive stop-weighting and logprob fallback behavior. Opt-in stream heartbeat to mitigate proxy-induced disconnects. See docs/migration/v1-compat.md for migration steps and legacy_stop_mode flag.
notes_for_ops: Rolling deploy: ensure worker nodes pick up new param_bridge config. The heartbeat config is stored under runtime.stream.heartbeat.enabled and defaults to false. If enabling in production, monitor connection churn dashboard and set heartbeat interval >= 15s.
changelog_excerpt: Implement v1 param bridge + toolcall framing. Add stream heartbeat and logprob provenance header. Backcompat guarded behind v1_compat flag.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for mapping logic (100% coverage for param_bridge), integration tests for framed toolcall reassembly, and e2e simulation verifying stream keepalive prevents proxy closures. CI passed on final run.
